title: Hybrid geo-pin with adaptive latency thresholds and predictive load-shedding
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Problem statement: We need a stable, predictable routing policy that balances latency SLOs, customer geography preferences, and regional capacity signals. Current strategies either over-pin (leading to hot regions) or over-hedge (higher p99 tail latency and cross-region egress). This ticket designs and implements a hybrid policy that combines soft geo-pinning with adaptive latency thresholds and predictive load-shedding while integrating region-level circuit breakers.
background: Customers expect regionally consistent latency (SLO: P95 < 120ms for short-form queries) and predictable throughput for Dedicated clusters. When regional load spikes or degraded hardware occurs, naive failover creates thundering herd effects in fallback regions. We observed repeated incidents where downstream regions hit capacity and global tail latency degraded. We need a routing policy that: 1) prefers local region for pinned customers, 2) falls back quickly and safely when local region violates SLO/capacity, 3) avoids creating new hotspots, and 4) exposes operator controls and metrics for gradual rollout.
proposal: Design a policy engine with three coordinated components: (A) Soft geo-pin layer: requests include a geo_pin preference with a TTL and staleness score; the policy prefers pinned region while allowing measured deviation. Pins are 'soft' — they can be overridden when region-level signals cross thresholds. (B) Latency SLO guardrails: per-region adaptive thresholds derived from rolling SLO slack (e.g., P95 observed vs target) and short-window increase detectors. If observed tail exceeds adaptive threshold, the region is marked 'degrade' for N seconds. (C) Capacity-aware steering & predictive shedding: use existing capacity telemetry (inflight requests, queue length, GPU util) plus a short-term predictive model to decide when to steer traffic away or shed non-essential requests (low-priority batch / non-interactive calls). Circuit breakers will open progressively: soft-reroute -> 10% spill -> 50% spill -> full reject to avoid cascading failures.
decision_rationale: Soft pins respect customer locality (latency, compliance) but must not be absolute. Adaptive thresholds reduce manual tuning and let us fail earlier on rising tail latency. Predictive shedding reduces load before queues saturate, minimizing tail amplification. Progressive circuit breaker stages provide visible degradation phases operators can observe and roll back if needed.
implementation_notes:
- Add new fields to request metadata: geo_pin (region code), pin_ttl, pin_priority. Backwards compatible default: no pin.
- Policy engine implemented as a routing middleware in the request proxy (edge layer). It consumes: per-region metrics from metrics API, realtime capacity hints from Dedicated scheduler, and model-inferred short-term load forecast.
- Expose a config schema for pin behavior: hard_limit_ms, soft_ttl_seconds, spill_percentages_by_stage.
- Circuit breakers: implement token-bucket style admission control per-region with metrics exported to Console (per-route breakdowns).
- Load-shedding: support annotation on routes for shedding class (e.g., "best-effort", "interactive"). Shedding only kicks in for non-interactive classes or when operator enables experimental mode for controlled tests.
- Telemetry: emit events when a request deviates from pin, when circuit breaker transitions, and when shedding occurs. Include reason codes for downstream analysis and SLO-linked alerts.
- Rollout: staged feature flag per-account and per-route; start with internal accounts then public beta.
acceptance_criteria: Routing middleware can read geo_pin metadata and apply soft-pin heuristics in simulations
Adaptive per-region latency thresholds computed and visualized in Console for last 30 days
Progressive circuit breaker stages trigger correctly under synthetic overload tests (unit tests + chaos tests)
Load-shedding respects route annotations and rejects or reroutes only when configured thresholds are crossed
No more than 5% increase in p50 while reducing p99 tail in fallback scenarios during canary runs
Operator can toggle policy per-customer via Console and observe clear metrics and events
observability_and_metrics: Minimum metrics to add: region_pin_hits, region_pin_overrides, region_degrade_state{0|1}, circuit_breaker_stage, shed_count_by_route, steer_decisions_by_region, predicted_spill_risk. Dashboards: per-tenant route breakdown showing pin compliance, spill percentages, and SLO slack. Alerts: persistent region_degrade_state > 30s and spill_rate > 20% should page infra on-call.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring function and TTL logic. 2) Integration tests in staging with pre-recorded traffic traces to validate steer decisions. 3) Chaos experiments: kill a region's serving process and verify graceful spill and rate-limited failover. 4) Traffic-surge simulation: generate synthetic requests to validate progressive circuit-breaker behavior. 5) Customer-facing beta: route 5 internal customers through new policy for 2 weeks and collect telemetry.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: internal sim and canary (engineering org)
Phase 1: opt-in beta for Dedicated customers (feature flag)
Phase 2: gradual ramp to all customers with automated rollback thresholds (if overall p99 increases or spill_rate > configured limit)
Phase 3: GA and docs in Console and API references.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive shedding might reject important requests — mitigation: require explicit per-route annotation for shedding and conservative default behavior. Risk: oscillation between regions under marginal capacity — mitigation: add cooldown windows and use predictive smoothing on steering percentages. Risk: inaccurate forecasts leading to preemptive shedding — mitigation: default to reactive thresholds and use ML predictions only as advisory until validated.
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Serving, and Console teams. Agreed on soft-pin semantics and instrumentation events.
2026-02-28: Prototype scoring function implemented; initial simulation shows 18% reduction in cross-region egress for pinned traffic.
2026-03-04: Implemented adaptive threshold logic and basic circuit-breaker stages in staging; began chaos tests.
2026-03-08: Observed stable failover in region kill test; noted that cooldown window needs tuning (increasing from 10s to 45s).
notes: This ticket pairs with a separate UX task in Console to display pin status and allow manual override — coordination required with PM/Design. Consider future extension for per-model pinning and compliance-tagged pins for data residency use cases.
